title: Embedding model regression fence and tenant-aware traffic sculpting playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Create a reproducible, telemetry-driven playbook for onboarding new embedding model variants and deprecating old ones with an explicit regression fence and tenant-aware traffic sculpting to protect latency SLOs and semantic quality.

Background: We run many tenant workloads with tight latency and quality budgets. Prior model swaps caused surprise semantic regressions and tail-latency spikes for a subset of tenants. This ticket captures the end-to-end onboarding + versioning playbook: candidate validation, gated dark-launch, selective canarying, tenant cohort rollout, automated rollback gates, and an operator runbook for deprecation.

Scope: rollout and rollback policies, telemetry signals and thresholds, automated traffic shaping hooks, integration points with Console (dashboards & rollouts), required smoke/regression tests, per-tenant throttling and opt-out flow, and deprecation timeline templates. Not in scope: model training pipelines and release-of-model-artifacts to external registries.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible rollout plan that can be executed from Console or via API with defined stages: validation, dark-launch, small canary, tenant cohort ramp, full ramp, and deprecation schedule.
Automated telemetry gates that block ramp at quality or latency regressions defined in signals list below.
Per-tenant traffic sculpting implemented: ability to pin, quarantine, or throttle tenant traffic to previous model variant with a single API call.
Regression fence tests (semantic/regression suite) with pass/fail thresholds and nightly auto-evals for candidate models.
Documentation and a one-pager runbook linked in Console and shared with SRE/Support teams.
Two staging rehearsals executed with synthetic tenant workloads and results recorded in the release dashboard.
Rollback automation triggered by either telemetry fence breach or manual operator action that reverts traffic within 5 minutes for 95% of tenants.
Stakeholder sign-off from Product and DevRel on semantic quality for top-10 customers during canary phase.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - Pre-validate: Run offline semantic probes and resource cost estimator on representative workloads; required: pass semantic stable score >= 0.98 vs baseline.
Stage 1 - Dark launch: Serve <0.5% of traffic in shadow mode capturing predictions, latencies, and embeddings for offline scoring.
Stage 2 - Micro canary: 1-5% traffic to a controlled tenant cohort selected by risk tier; monitor fences for 24h.
Stage 3 - Cohort ramp: Gradually increase to 25% across heterogeneous tenants with tenant-aware throttle policies; keep cohort isolation for 48h.
Stage 4 - Broad ramp: 25% -> 75% over 72h if passing gates; enable cost/latency optimizations like quantized kernel paths where allowed.
Stage 5 - Full: 100% routing; start deprecation countdown for old model and publish migration notes.
Stage 6 - Sunset: After 30 days stable, remove old model variant and update catalog; archive audit logs.
Stage - Emergency rollback: Immediately pin tenant to previous variant and notify on-call; automated rollback should complete within SLO.
Stage - Opt-out: Provide per-tenant opt-out API for 90 days after full ramp for customers that request extended validation.
telemetry_signals: p95 latency per tenant and global: block if increase >20% over baseline for 1h
p99 tail latency: block if increase >30% or absolute >800ms for text embeddings workload
semantic drift: median cosine similarity to goldset; block if median drops >0.03
recall@10/recall@100 on seeded rerank evals: block if relative drop >5%
KL divergence on embedding distribution buckets: block if divergence >0.04
error rate (responses with server errors) increase >2x
memory pressure / OOM events on GPU nodes
per-tenant quality-lag fence computed from tenant-specific eval subset
inference QPS and per-GPU throughput vs provisioning: spike >25% leading to autoscaler thrash
migration_steps: 1) Prep candidate: produce model artifacts, generate quantization artifacts and perf profiles.
2) Register model in catalog with version tag and compatibility metadata (seq len, kv-cache footprint, quantization-ready).
3) Run full semantic and perf probe suite in staging; record baselines in release dashboard.
4) Start Stage 1 dark-launch, capture traces and embeddings for offline regressions.
5) If dark-launch passes, proceed to micro canary and enable per-tenant telemetry export for cohort.
6) Use traffic-sculptor API to pin or throttle tenants showing regressions to prior variant.
7) Execute broad ramp with gated autoscaler hints and kernel selection flags tuned for the model.
8) After stable window, announce deprecation and start sunset workflow (docs, migrations, billing adjustments if applicable).
risks: Semantic regression for niche tenants (long-tail prompts) not covered by global eval sets.
Tail-latency regressions triggered by new kernel/attention changes under specific seq-length distribution.
Capacity mis-estimation leading to degraded latency for bursty tenants during ramp.
Rollback flakiness if cache warming differs between variants causing user-visible instability.
Operational complexity for teams to manage per-tenant throttles and opt-outs at scale.
mitigation_actions: Maintain tenant-specific evaluation subsets and run targeted probes before cohort ramp.
Add lightweight canary microbenchmarks for seq-length slices that previously exposed tail spikes.
Integrate autoscaler safety buffers and apply staged node warm-up hooks when ramp increases capacity demand.
Implement dual-warmup: prime KV caches for candidate variant in dark-launch to reduce divergence in live response latencies.
Create a small operator UI in Console to manage tenant quarantines and visualize per-tenant gates.
